blocks.p: Angel drives the station wagon back to the Fossoil. This chapter explains the dashboard and the *Enter Vehicle* window.

While you drive, the dashboard of the car sits at the foot of the screen. Each car has a dashboard drawn to match it; Figure 5-1 shows the station wagon's. The fuel gauge is at the left end, and its needle shows the fuel in the tank.
Angel's wagon comes in with its tank all but empty: the needle of the fuel gauge is on *E*. Chapter 10 shows how to refuel it.
The speedometer in the middle reads in miles per hour above and in kilometers per hour below, with the odometer under it. The temperature gauge is at the right of the speedometer.
Along the foot of the dashboard are the switches, each named on the panel: *LIGHTS*, *LOCK*, *TAILGATE*, *WIPER* and *CRUISE*. The key turns from *OFF* to *ON* and *START*.

blocks.p: The *Enter Vehicle* window, in Figure 5-2, shows the seats of the car from above, each with its number. The heading names the seat under the pointer, and the help line at the foot of the window says what a click does: here, *Take this seat: Driver.* Seat 1 is the driver's seat.
Click a seat to take it. To drive, take the driver's seat. Seats 1 and 2 are the front seats and seats 3 and 4 the back seats.

Every window of ZNIX, the small ones too, ends in a help line. With the mouse, the help line gives the plain-words help for what the pointer is over; when the pointer is over nothing, it gives the window's own status. The help line holds one line; a longer help is cut short with an ellipsis.

blocks.note: On a controller, the help line shows the prompts for what has focus instead: the pad buttons and what each one does.

blocks.p: To close the window without taking a seat, click *Cancel*.
